status_semantics.observed_original: Original finding establishes only the named observed paths; tools tests additionally verify rejection/bounds.
status_semantics.tooling_tested: Inspected implementation and public synthetic tests; no original gameplay capability promotion.
status_semantics.unsupported: Explicit adapter backlog; reject typed requests.
status_semantics.not_present: Native extension beyond the inspected emulator interface.

emulator.scope: Reset, guarded startup dispatch, original Kernel loop and original field loader; no checkpoint prerequisite. Kernel observed on both exact profiles; initialized fields 14 on Disc 1 and 15 on Disc 2 do not imply universal scene coverage.

Exact CHD profile; source raw-track/index/catalog fingerprints and field-slot formula checked. Numeric field availability is not semantic validity or entry-script completion. Dummy/absent/relabelled pairs rejected.
Three named presets, JSON-path scenarios, numeric --map, explicit --profile and overrides; --list and --dry-run compile without emulation. Only kernel and field entry types.

Kernel or selected map plus two original initialization indicators stable for two frontend boundaries; timeout default 5000 (1..30000); settle default 120 (1..3600). Only ready: map. Not player-control readiness.

Ordered 14 digital button names; hold default 8 (1..3600), release all then after default 60 (1..30000); wait 1..30000. At most 100 scenario steps. Counts are retro_run calls, not recovered logical ticks; empty button arrays allowed.

Expected/value equal-length lowercase bytes; all guards tested before writes; no overlaps and launcher controls protected; 2 MiB physical RAM bounds. Custom field writes become analysis_probe, not typed progression; kernel custom writes rejected.

Lower-level observe --program supports bounded RAM width 1/2/4, masked eq/ne/lt/le/gt/ge and stable frames at pre-retro_run boundaries. It is an analysis interface, not live breakpoint/watchpoint control.
Compiled total budget <=36000 frontend calls; individual executor steps also bounded. Actual readiness timeout recorded as failure. No independent worker-hang wall watchdog in this runner.

Requested step images/RAM plus periodic 600-frame captures; accumulated audio and final external-core state. Capture is original output with hashes, not structured native introspection or an attachable live spectator stream. Captures always record card 1 (libretro save RAM) as card1.mcd with its hash and card 2's file hash; an optional exact 128 KiB --card image is inserted as card 1 before the first frame and recorded in provenance. Under the HLE BIOS card 2 formats and saves; card 1 formatting fails in the pinned core.

Normalized scenario/program/catalog, started hashes, compiler/executor/core/BIOS/source/Nix identities, options and ordered condition/write events; private new .local output. Only successful report.json means completion; runtime errors write capture/failure.json. Preflight rejects may occur before capture creation.

Pinned external interpreter avoids stale translated instructions after guarded code writes; default HLE explicitly labeled. Optional supplied BIOS hashed; detected HLE fallback rejected. Neither HLE nor core output is hardware equivalence.

observe --load-state can validate same content/core/BIOS/options and captured state hash; scenario.py deliberately always cold-boots. Final external state is not portable native serialization or proof of deterministic full-game replay.

--sample-memory optional bounded read-only direct or one-pointer RAM sampling after prior retro_run and before scenario tick; re-resolves aliases and reports null/out-of-range reads. <=32 ranges, 8192 bytes/sample, 64 MiB payload, 1 million range records. Scope here is tested tooling, not full semantic state coverage.

--trace-instructions optionally observes guarded interpreter PCs, registers and bounded RAM ranges without writes. Optional region digests use explicit bounds, rejecting invalid pointers, alias wrapping and excessive hashing work. Limits: 128 hooks, one million candidate callbacks, 64 MiB per-hook emitted payload bound and separate 64 MiB hashing-work bound. Optional --coverage windows (1..1024 ordered frame windows, 1..16 word-aligned code ranges) record every dispatched RAM word with its first and last fetched instruction word and a changed flag, and hash the code ranges at each window start and end, read-only. No interactive debugger or hardware timing claim. The versionless trace interface also exposes read-only 1 KiB scratchpad backing for register-relative ranges at physical, KSEG0 and KSEG1 aliases. Cross-boundary ranges and hardware-register addresses are rejected. Direct ranges, pointer_offset ranges and digests remain RAM-only. The collector and extension share one callback signature without version discovery or version metadata. Optional snapshot hooks (paired with max_snapshots, at most 8192) store the complete 2 MiB RAM and 1 KiB scratchpad backing at a guarded PC in a file beside the trace, as a full keyframe every 256 snapshots and otherwise only the 256-byte pages changed since the previous snapshot; per-record digests verify every reconstructed image; they remain read-only observations and do not attribute writes made by interrupt handlers. A hook's optional vram register names a RECT whose VRAM pixels the record reads through retro_xem_vram_read (the GPU plugin's save-state export; at most 64 MiB per capture). Each record also carries the 64 raw GTE words (32 data, then 32 control) as the pinned interpreter stores them; the hook reads them without writing emulated state. Snapshots also store the 4 KiB hardware I/O register page (1f801000) read through the same read-only hardware backing pointer; register state is an observation, not emulated memory.

Player/party position and facing adapter unrecovered; typed fields rejected. Need actor identity, units, initialization order and collision-safe spawn evidence. Guarded raw probes do not establish support.
Typed party, stats, equipment, inventory, flags and progression unrecovered/rejected. Native must add typed dependent initialization for every supported subsystem, not inherit this limit.

Direct battle/formation launch is not a recovered scenario entry. Kernel Battle-mode research in EVID-REF-013 is an analysis probe with unresolved valid setup/readiness/return, not a supported battle adapter.

World map, Battling, movie and event-specific entry lack dedicated recovered adapters; observed Kernel labels do not prove valid parameterization/readiness. Native adds world-map, minigame, event and semantic menu entry as systems arrive.
Player-control, actionable dialogue/menu, script-completion and battle-ready predicates unavailable; ready values other than map rejected. Native must distinguish them from asset/map initialization.
No discoverable live semantic agent API, analog actions, concurrent inspectors, controller handoff or cancellation service in scenario runner. Native protocol adds them over the actual shared engine.

Runner executes bounded frontend frames without realtime pacing in its Python loop; it does not expose recovered exact simulation ticks, real-time/fixed/unlocked mode selection, wall watchdog or throughput contract.
Static emulator captures exist; no optional attachable read-only native image stream, queue/drop policy or presentation-independent state-equivalence proof.

No complete native semantic state schemas, transactional native editing, portable snapshots, native/Lua task stepping, native debugger integration or both-disc typed full-game go-anywhere. These remain mandatory native extensions.

maintenance: Any baseline source drift fails repository validation. Inspect changes, extend rows/tests, update source hashes and bump parity_version. Native passes require their own platform evidence; no emulator backlog promotion from native implementation.

change_review.author: Claude Opus 5.5
change_review.scope: 1.10.0: Reviewed VRAM read-backs and the larger hook table of the trace extension. nix/reference-trace.h exports retro_xem_vram_read, which copies a VRAM rectangle through the GPU plugin's save-state export (GPU_freeze(1), the call a save state makes; it completes buffered commands and writes no VRAM, RAM or CPU state), and accepts up to 128 hook PCs behind a PC bitmap filter; the interpreter hook points are unchanged. tools/reference/instruction_trace.py accepts a hook's vram register (the RECT address), records rect, sha256 and hex or why the rectangle is unavailable, and bounds a capture's VRAM reads to 64 MiB. Tests in tests/test_instruction_trace.py cover 128 hooks, the read, rectangles outside VRAM, a rejected read and missing exports. p1shared-transition-chain (107 hooks, VRAM at _drs 800462dc) reproduced the final RAM of p1shared-transition-reload. Refreshed live baseline hashes; native methods remain unimplemented. Previous review: 1.9.0: Reviewed the coverage mode of the trace extension. nix/reference-trace.h keeps, per aligned RAM word, an executed bit, a changed bit and the first and last fetched instruction word, exported through retro_xem_coverage_enable and retro_xem_coverage_take (copy then clear); the interpreter hook points are unchanged. tools/reference/instruction_trace.py (validate_coverage, CoverageTrace, read_coverage_records, split_coverage) validates the window/range specification, stores one zlib record per window and hashes the declared code ranges at each window boundary; observe.py and scenario.py accept --coverage. CoverageTests in tests/test_instruction_trace.py cover window lifecycle, record layout, missing exports, rejected transfers, bounds and corrupt files. The 18 p1cov coverage captures reproduced the final RAM of earlier captures of the same routes, 11 of them from the uninstrumented core. Refreshed live baseline hashes; native methods remain unimplemented.
